sourceLabel: Audited consolidated financial results filed with the exchanges
coverage: Reported business segments · segment income before inter-segment revenue
profitMetric: Segment result (profit before finance costs, tax and unallocated items)
definition: Each segment’s profit before finance costs, interest income, other unallocated income and expense, exceptional items and tax. The two rows add up to ₹17,591.65 crore. After finance costs, interest income and other unallocated items this becomes profit before exceptional items and tax of ₹15,056.26 crore. It is not profit after tax.
location: PDF page 18 (note 3, consolidated segment revenue and results, year ended March 31, 2026 column), PDF page 15 (consolidated results) and PDF page 20 (note 7); the filing has no printed page numbers
notes: Port and SEZ activities means developing, operating and maintaining port services, port-related infrastructure and infrastructure at the contiguous Special Economic Zone. Segment income of ₹38,970.60 crore is before ₹234.83 crore of inter-segment revenue; after it, revenue from operations is ₹38,735.77 crore. Total income, including other income of ₹2,118.59 crore, is ₹40,854.36 crore. Group profit after tax is ₹12,782.03 crore: profit before tax ₹14,848.56 crore less tax ₹2,066.53 crore. Of it, ₹12,806.21 crore belongs to owners of the company and −₹24.18 crore to minority owners of subsidiaries. Profit is after exceptional costs of ₹207.70 crore (note 7): ₹145.64 crore for the new Labour Codes (higher employee retirement-pay liability) and ₹62.06 crore to settle a voluntary retirement plan at a foreign subsidiary. Profit includes a ₹257.62 crore share of profit from joint ventures. The filing does not disclose profit for any single port or terminal.
insight: Ports and the special economic zone earn almost all of the segment profit, and a much larger share of each rupee of income than the logistics business. Finance costs are a large deduction on the way to the group profit.
